title: Reservation eligibility lattice and staggered provisioning with surge buffer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a deterministic decision lattice for reservation intake and a staggered provisioning flow that combines steady committed capacity with a managed surge buffer. This ticket covers the policy, API contract, and orchestration steps that translate a reservation request into an approved commitment, a provisioning schedule, and autoscaling knobs.

Background: Customers requesting Dedicated capacity need both predictable throughput SLAs and operational flexibility to handle short-term spikes. Current intake reviews are manual and create bursty onboarding that strains fleet controls. We need a structured eligibility model that encodes business rules (commitment term, expected sustained RPS, burst tolerance, credit score, regional constraints) and maps to a provisioning plan that phases capacity allocation (initial probation slice, steady commit, and a reclaimable surge buffer).

Key deliverables:
- Reservation eligibility lattice doc (rules + scoring + overrides) and permissive/strict modes.
- API additions to reservation intake: eligibility_reason, provisional_allocation, surge_budget, probation_window and scheduled_activation_time.
- Orchestration plan for phased provisioning (0-72h probation, steady ramp, surge reclaim policies).
- Autoscaling policy templates that combine reserved pool and ephemeral surge instances with SLA-preserving fallback (model variant downgrade or regional spillover).
- Console UI mockups to show staged allocation and countdowns (Figma link below).
- Acceptance criteria: automated decision path for >=80% of intake requests, end-to-end tests exercising allocation and reclaim flows, and billing/accounting signals that reflect provisional vs committed capacity.

Integration points:
- Console (reservation detail + approve/reject UI) - UX lead: Lena Chen (design).
- Billing & metering (reflect provisional vs committed tokens) - Finance + Billing APIs.
- Fleet controller (k8s autoscaler hooks + capacity ledger) - ENG runtime.
- SLA generator (commitment -> SLA doc) - Legal/Support templates.

Links and artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/reservation-eligibility-lattice
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcdef/staged-provisioning
- Spec draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xY_spec_draft
- Reference GH branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6842

Risks and open questions:
- How to price provisional surge? (flat premium vs usage-based). Open: pricing PM to finalize.
- Edge case: concurrent reservations that compete for the same regional pool during onboarding windows. Need conflict resolution policy (first-commit, priority-based, or fairness window).
- Monitoring: we need new metrics for provisional_allocation_utilization and surge_reclaim_rate.

Next steps:
1) Finalize eligibility lattice and publish to Confluence (owner: Miguel).
2) Schema review with runtime and billing teams for API changes (owner: Aisha).
3) Prototype orchestration in a staging fleet and run chaos tests for reclaiming surge (owner: ENG - runtime).
